lines.text: Shipping a release means build, then test, then docs, then deploy. Four agents, and a human nudging every single one.
Each handoff waits for you. You check the board, copy the context, and start the next task by hand.
Agent R Q events fix that. An event is a named signal that a task sends the moment it finishes.
Build completes and emits built. Test completes and emits tested. The agent calls nothing, it only reports what happened.
Wire each event to the next workspace, and the next task appears on its own. No glue code at all.
The tester is already listening. The moment built lands, it picks the task up and starts working.
Events can fan out too. One built signal starts testing and docs at the same time, so they run in parallel.
You stay in control. Deploy keeps its approval, so the train never ships without a human saying yes.
Add a schedule, and the whole train leaves at two in the morning while you sleep.
If a step fails, the train stops right there, and you can see exactly which stop it was.
Every handoff lands in the task timeline, so you can always see what fired what, and when.
No glue code, no copy and paste. Try events at Agent R Q dot com.
